validated_work_order.understanding: Posting a scheduled transaction and then moving that transaction's date to an earlier day makes the schedule reappear as an un-posted row in the register and flips its status from 'Paid' back to 'Due'. Whether an occurrence counts as paid is decided by a DATE COMPARISON, not by the existence of a linked transaction: getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate returns schedule.next_date itself as the lower bound whenever the date condition op is 'is' (packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts:94-97), and both callers then require the transaction to fall at or after that bound - getHasTransactionsQuery with a one-sided `date: { $gte }` (schedules.ts:165-193) and isScheduleOccurrencePosted with `>= matchStartDate && <= occurrenceDate` (schedules.ts:130-152). Posting creates the transaction dated exactly next_date, so it matches; editing the date to any earlier day moves it below the bound, the query stops matching, hasTrans goes false, getStatus falls back to comparing next_date with today (schedules.ts:52-76) and returns 'due', and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions regenerates the row because 'due' is in the isForPreview list (schedules.ts:425-434). I reproduced this end to end in Chromium against http://localhost:3001 today (2026-10-02) using the demo budget: 'Phone bills' (Dominion Power, Bank of America, 120.00, date condition op 'is', monthly on the 2nd) read 'Due'; after 'Post transaction' it read 'Paid' and the register dropped the schedule row; after clicking that transaction's date cell and setting 09/25/2026 (SEVEN days early) the register brought the row straight back as '10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Phone bills | Due | 120.00' alongside the real linked transaction, and the Schedules page flipped 'Paid' -> 'Due'. No console errors and no page errors at any step. The lower bound is the wrong SHAPE: the gap between next_date and the real payment date is a property of how early the user paid, not a constant. THE REJECTED PLAN (v3) kept that shape but derived the bound from the recurrence INTERVAL ([previousOccurrence + 1 day, D]), and I have now confirmed by execution that it is wrong for a different reason than the reviewer gave - see objection 1 below.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Whether a schedule occurrence counts as paid is decided by comparing a linked transaction's date against a lower bound derived from schedule.next_date, rather than by the existence of that transaction: getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate returns next_date itself as the lower bound for every date condition with op 'is' (schedules.ts:94-97), so a payment made even one day early falls below the bound, hasTrans goes false, and getStatus reverts to a date comparison against today while the transaction stays linked to the schedule throughout.
validated_work_order.approach: Widen the lower bound, but widen it by a BOUNDED early-payment GRACE WINDOW rather than by a whole recurrence interval. For a recurring schedule whose date condition op is 'is', the match window for occurrence D becomes [D - grace, D], where grace = min(7 days, recurrenceIntervalDays - 1). Everything else keeps exact-date matching: posts_transaction schedules, one-time (string) date values, and any frequency not in the interval table; schedules with no date condition keep the existing 2-day lookback. ANSWERING OBJECTION 1 DIRECTLY, because it is correct and v3 did not answer it: the reviewer's argument is that getHasTransactionsQuery is ONE-SIDED (schedules.ts:165-193 has `date: { $gte }` and no `$lte`), so widening its lower bound without an upper bound admits a transaction belonging to the PREVIOUS occurrence. I confirmed this by execution - I emulated v3's bound (previous occurrence + 1 day, computed from a shifted recurrence start) against the real Condition/RSchedule pipeline and ran the real advanceSchedulesService: with a monthly schedule at next_date 2026-11-02 and a linked transaction dated 2026-10-20 (a LATE payment of the October bill), v3's bound yields `$gte: 2026-10-03`, the status flips 'scheduled' -> 'paid', and next_date is advanced to 2026-12-02 - November is skipped permanently, never projected and never posted. Today's code leaves next_date at 2026-11-02. So the reviewer's failure mode is real. I did NOT adopt the reviewer's option (a), an explicit `$lte: schedule.next_date`, because the reviewer correctly notes it is not equivalent to today's behaviour and I agree it is a REGRESSION in the other direction: today a transaction dated AFTER next_date still matches, which is exactly how a missed occurrence paid today reads as paid (the 'keeps a schedule posted today paid for the rest of the day' case at packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.test.ts:989). Adding `$lte` would make a late payment invisible and leave the bill unpaid forever. I also did not adopt option (b), keeping exact-date matching for getHasTransactionsQuery and widening only the two-sided callers, because it does not satisfy AC-1/AC-2: the Schedules page reaches 'paid' through useSchedules.ts:34, whose `liveQuery(getHasTransactionsQuery(schedules), ...)` feeds `hasTrans` straight into getStatus, so an unchanged getHasTransactionsQuery leaves the Schedules page showing 'Due' after the re-date - exactly the reproduced symptom. THE FIX: make the grace window smaller than the recurrence interval, which is what makes the ONE-SIDED query sound without an upper bound. Because grace <= interval - 1, the widened lower bound for occurrence D can never reach back past the previous occurrence D-interval, so a transaction late for the previous occurrence cannot cross it; and because grace is capped at 7 days, a transaction dated ON OR AFTER next_date - which today's one-sided query already matches, with no upper bound - continues to match, preserving the late-payment behaviour the reviewer flagged. So the fix is a strict WIDENING of an already-open-ended window by at most 7 days, never reaching into the previous occurrence. MEASURED, running the real getHasTransactionsQuery, getStatus and advanceSchedulesService against a scratch database (all four end-to-end, monthly start 2026-10-02, next_date forced to 2026-11-02, posts_transaction false): (A) transaction re-dated to 2026-10-26, SEVEN days early - the reporter's scenario - reports paid true; (B) transaction dated 2026-10-20, a LATE payment of the October bill - the reviewer's counter-scenario - reports paid false and leaves next_date at 2026-11-02 rather than advancing to 2026-12-02, which is the regression test the reviewer required and which v3 FAILS; (C) transaction dated exactly 2026-11-02 reports paid true; (D) transaction dated 2026-11-10, AFTER next_date, still reports paid true and still advances next_date to 2026-12-02, preserving today's late-payment behaviour that option (a) would have broken. MEASURED per frequency, using a local probe of the window arithmetic: daily (interval 1) gets grace 0, so occurrence 2024-03-10 -> bound 2024-03-10 and 2024-03-11 -> 2024-03-11, and a transaction dated 2024-03-10 satisfies exactly ['2024-03-10'] and not ['2024-03-11']; weekly (interval 7) gets grace 6, so a Monday-start series (2024-01-01 weekly) gives occurrence 2024-03-04 -> bound 2024-02-27, and a transaction dated 2024-03-04 satisfies exactly one of ['2024-02-26','2024-03-04','2024-03-11'], namely ['2024-03-04'], so adjacent weekly windows do not share a boundary date; monthly gets grace 7 and yearly grace 7. Read the interval from the date condition value's `frequency` and `interval ?? 1`, never by reverse-iterating the recurrence - unlike v3 this needs no Condition construction, no rschedule iteration, and no date-fns subtraction at all, so v3's stated cost risk (a new per-schedule recurrence lookup in a query that maps over every schedule) disappears. It also sidesteps v3's measured monthUtils.subMonths day-loss trap and v3's untested skipWeekend and dual-rrule unknowns entirely, because the bound no longer depends on where the recurrence's raw occurrences fall. ANSWERING OBJECTION 2 DIRECTLY: every case in tests[] below now states its recurrence start, frequency, interval, patterns and endMode explicitly, and every expected bound is re-derivable by hand from the stated rule `bound = D - min(7, intervalDays - 1)` with no reference to a recurrence lookup at all. The reviewer's weekly example is corrected as they specify: start 2024-01-01, frequency weekly, interval 1, patterns [], no endMode; occurrence 2024-03-04; grace 6; bound 2024-02-27.

files.change: In getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate (currently lines 90-102), replace the bare `return occurrenceDate` inside the `dateCond?.op === 'is'` branch with a bounded early-payment grace window. Add a module-level constant mapping recurrence frequency to its nominal interval length in days - `{ daily: 1, weekly: 7, monthly: 28, yearly: 365 }` - and a module-level constant `EARLY_PAYMENT_GRACE_DAYS = 7`. Inside the op === 'is' branch: if `dateCond.value` is not an object (a one-time schedule with a string date) return `occurrenceDate` unchanged; otherwise read `frequency` and `interval ?? 1` from that value, look up the interval length, and if the frequency is absent from the table return `occurrenceDate` unchanged; otherwise compute `grace = Math.max(0, Math.min(EARLY_PAYMENT_GRACE_DAYS, intervalLength * interval - 1))` and return `monthUtils.subDays(occurrenceDate, grace)`. Note the argument order: `monthUtils.subDays` is `(day: DateLike, n: number)` (packages/loot-core/src/shared/months.ts:239) - the arguments are NOT reversed. Keep the `posts_transaction` short-circuit and the trailing 2-day lookback exactly as they are, and keep the order of checks so `posts_transaction` is still evaluated for schedules that have a date condition. Do NOT reverse-iterate the recurrence, do NOT construct a Condition, and do NOT use date-fns or monthUtils.subMonths for this computation - the bound is pure interval arithmetic. Rewrite the doc comment above getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate (currently lines 83-89, which says 'Used by getHasTransactionsQuery for `next_date` (lower bound only)') to state the corrected contract: the returned date is the INCLUSIVE lower bound of the match window for that occurrence, which is `[D - min(7 days, recurrenceIntervalDays - 1), D]` for a recurring op-'is' schedule and exactly `D` otherwise; the grace is capped below the recurrence interval so the window for occurrence D can never reach into the previous occurrence, which is what keeps the ONE-SIDED `$gte` in getHasTransactionsQuery from matching a transaction that belongs to an earlier occurrence; and because that query has no upper bound, a transaction dated on or after D still matches, so a late payment continues to read as paid. Update the equivalent comment above getHasTransactionsQuery (lines 154-164), which currently states '`dateCond.op === "is"` (one-time or recurring): exact `next_date`, no lookback', to describe the grace window and to state explicitly that the query is intentionally one-sided and that the grace bound, not an upper bound, is what keeps it correct. Do not add `// @ts-strict-ignore` to any new file and do not remove the existing marker at line 1 of this file.
files.why: This single helper is the lower bound for all three callers - getHasTransactionsQuery (used by useSchedules.ts:34 for the Schedules page and by advanceSchedulesService, which writes) and isScheduleOccurrencePosted (used by forecast-schedules). A bounded grace window fixes the reproduced bug for all three at once, keeps the one-sided query sound by construction rather than by the disjointness argument v3 used and got wrong for this caller, and needs no recurrence lookup.

qa_script: 1. `yarn start`, open $PREVIEW_URL, click 'Try the demo' on the welcome screen. This creates a 'Phone bills' schedule: Dominion Power, Bank of America, monthly on the 2nd, date condition op 'is', posts_transaction false, recurrence start EQUALS today so next_date is the series' FIRST occurrence (created by packages/loot-core/src/mocks/budget.ts:966-975). That first-occurrence property is the point: there is no preceding occurrence to look back to.
2. Go to Schedules. Confirm 'Phone bills' reads: Dominion Power | Bank of America | 10/02/2026 | Due | 120.00.
3. Right-click 'Phone bills' and choose 'Post transaction'. Confirm the Schedules page now shows status 'Paid' and that the Bank of America register no longer shows the 'Phone bills' schedule row.
4. Open Bank of America. The posted transaction reads 10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Categorize | 120.00.

5. Click that transaction's date cell and pick a date SEVEN DAYS before the original due date (09/25/2026). This is the reproduced gap, well beyond the two days the earlier rejected plan assumed. The date cell is inside a row carrying data-testid="row", with the date in a cell carrying data-testid="date"; clicking it turns the cell into a text input pre-filled with the current date, which you overwrite and confirm with Enter.

6. THE BUG, before the fix: the schedule row reappears in the register as '10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Phone bills | Due | 120.00' and the Schedules page flips from 'Paid' to 'Due'. After the fix, neither happens: the register shows only the posted transaction and the Schedules page still reads 'Paid'. Reload the page and confirm it stays 'Paid'.

7. Future-due variant, the reporter's own shape, INSIDE the grace window: back on Schedules, right-click 'Phone bills' > 'Skip next scheduled date' so next_date moves to 11/02/2026 (a ~31-day gap), post it, then re-date the posted transaction to 10/26/2026 - seven days early, which is exactly the monthly grace. The status must remain 'Paid' and no schedule row may reappear. Do NOT use 10/20/2026 here: that is 13 days early, outside the grace window, and is deliberately treated as a late payment of the PREVIOUS occurrence per AC-3 and AC-7.

8. Regression sweep, and the check that distinguishes this fix from the rejected one: (a) 'Skip next scheduled date' and 'Post transaction today' must still behave as before; (b) an auto-posted schedule (created with 'Automatically add transaction' enabled) must still match on its exact date; (c) a LATE payment still counts - re-date a posted transaction FORWARD past next_date (e.g. to 11/10/2026 for an occurrence of 11/02/2026) and confirm it still reads 'Paid', since the one-sided query has no upper bound and this is the behaviour an `$lte` upper bound would have broken; (d) a daily recurring schedule paid once must still project its later occurrences, so the forecast does not double-count.
risks: THE 7-DAY GRACE IS A PRODUCT CALL, now scoped rather than deferred: a bill paid more than 7 days before its due date still shows as unpaid. This is deliberate and is the same bound that prevents the one-sided getHasTransactionsQuery from matching a transaction belonging to the previous occurrence, so the two cannot be tuned independently - widening the grace past roughly half the shortest recurrence interval would start crediting late payments of the previous occurrence. The window is one constant (EARLY_PAYMENT_GRACE_DAYS) and is asserted in tests, so changing it later is a one-line edit.

The fix deliberately does NOT add an `$lte` upper bound to getHasTransactionsQuery, because today a transaction dated after next_date still matches and that is how a missed occurrence paid today reads as paid (packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.test.ts:989). Soundness rests on the grace being smaller than the recurrence interval, which is asserted for daily, weekly and monthly in schedules.test.ts and end-to-end through advanceSchedulesService in app.test.ts.

getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate now branches on the date condition value's `frequency` and `interval` fields. If a value carries a frequency the interval table does not list, the code falls back to exact-date matching, which is today's behaviour and cannot regress anything - but it means an unlisted frequency silently gets no grace. The unrecognised-frequency case is asserted so the fallback is deliberate.

Monthly schedules carrying BOTH day-of-month and day-of-week patterns expand into two separate rrules via recurConfigToRSchedule. This plan does not care: the bound is interval arithmetic over the declared frequency, so no rule expansion or occurrence iteration is involved. That is a material improvement over v3, whose bound depended on reverse-iterating the recurrence and left this case listed as an untested unknown.

skipWeekend is likewise a non-issue for this design: v3 could not guarantee a weekend-solved next_date aligned with a raw recurrence occurrence, whereas here the bound is computed from next_date directly and never consults the recurrence. A weekend-solved next_date therefore gets the same 7-day grace as any other monthly occurrence.

The grace is computed with monthUtils.subDays, whose signature is `(day: DateLike, n: number)` (packages/loot-core/src/shared/months.ts:239). v3 tripped over exactly this class of mistake with monthUtils.subMonths dropping the day; the argument order is stated explicitly in files[] so the implementer does not reverse it.

packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts is marked `// @ts-strict-ignore`. New code there inherits that; do not add the marker to any NEW file and do not remove the existing one as part of this change.

This change makes the Schedules page (useSchedules.ts:34) and the write path (advanceSchedulesService) agree on 'paid' where they previously did too, so no divergence is introduced. It does not restructure advanceSchedulesService.
out_of_scope: Whether posting a schedule whose due date is in the future should advance next_date at all is a separate design question. advanceSchedulesService only reaches its setNextDate branch for schedules already computed as 'paid' (packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts:747-762); this change does not restructure that service.

Covering a payment dated more than the grace window early, and covering a payment dated exactly on the previous occurrence's own date, both need a stamp recording which occurrence a transaction was posted from, not a wider window. Stated inside AC-3 rather than deferred.
The 'Utilities' (no payee, 1,900.00, Upcoming) and 'Wedding' schedules in the demo budget are unrelated to this ticket and were left alone.

The date-picker Save control in the schedule edit dialog did not commit a changed recurring date during reproduction, so the future-due scenario was set up with 'Skip next scheduled date' instead. That looks like a separate UI issue and is not investigated here.
No new product setting for a maximum early-payment window; the grace is a single constant with tests, so no setting is needed to change it.
No change to .sdlc/memory/**, docs/spec/**, docs/prd.md, docs/trd.md, docs/ui.md, .github/** or .sdlc/**.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: I reproduced the bug myself end to end in Chromium against $PREVIEW_URL with the demo budget, re-dating the posted transaction seven days early and observing both the resurrected register row and the Paid -> Due flip. Both review objections are answered with measurements rather than arguments. Objection 1 I confirmed by execution before designing around it: I emulated v3's recurrence-derived bound against the real Condition/RSchedule pipeline and the real advanceSchedulesService, and watched next_date jump from 2026-11-02 to 2026-12-02 because a late payment of the October bill was credited to November - the exact skip the reviewer predicted, so v3 is unsafe on its own fixture family. I then measured the fix I am specifying end to end through the real getHasTransactionsQuery, getStatus and advanceSchedulesService against a scratch database: the reporter's 7-days-early case reports paid, the reviewer's late-October case reports NOT paid and leaves next_date alone, a transaction dated exactly on next_date reports paid, and a transaction dated after next_date still reports paid and still advances - the last being the case that killed the reviewer's own option (a). I also ran the per-frequency window arithmetic (daily grace 0, weekly grace 6, monthly and yearly grace 7) through a scratch probe covering the repro, the objection-1 counter-case, late payments, the daily double-count guard, weekly boundary disjointness, auto-post precision, one-time schedules and the no-date-condition lookback: 7 of 7 passed. I established the existing-test impact by execution - the fix changes exactly two existing cases in schedules.test.ts, and I know their new values (2024-03-03, and false -> true for 'early pay day before due for recurring date cond') - and confirmed app.test.ts:989 still passes unmodified, which is why no upper bound is added. What I could not do: verify the fixed behaviour in the browser, because the debugger role forbids editing application code, so the browser check in qa_script is the implementer's to run. Confidence is high rather than certain only because the grace constant is a product judgement and because I have not measured the fix against a budget with a large number of schedules.
evidence: REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY against http://localhost:3001 (Chromium, fresh session, demo budget, no console or page errors at any step). Today is 2026-10-02.
Schedules page before posting: 'Phone bills | Dominion Power | Bank of America | 10/02/2026 | Due | ~ | 120.00'.
After 'Post transaction': status becomes 'Paid' and the register correctly drops the schedule row, showing '10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Categorize | 120.00'.

THE BUG, after clicking the posted transaction's date cell (a cell carrying data-testid="date" inside a row carrying data-testid="row") and overwriting the resulting text input with 09/25/2026, SEVEN days early: the register brings the schedule row back alongside the real linked transaction - '10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Phone bills | Due | 120.00' (resurrected) next to the real 'Dominion Power | Categorize | 120.00' transaction - and the Schedules page row for 'Phone bills' flips from 'Paid' to 'Due'.

OBJECTION 1 CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION, NOT BY REASONING. I emulated v3's bound (previous occurrence + 1 day, via a shifted recurrence start built with date-fns, the same shape v3 specified) and ran the real advanceSchedulesService against a scratch database. Monthly schedule, { start: '2026-10-02', frequency: 'monthly', patterns: [] }, next_date forced to 2026-11-02, one linked transaction dated 2026-10-20 - a LATE payment of the OCTOBER bill. Today's code: serialized filter `[{"$or":[{"$and":{"schedule":"id3","date":{"$gte":"2026-11-02"}}}]}]`, status 'scheduled', next_date stays 2026-11-02 - correct. v3's widened bound: filter `$gte: 2026-10-03`, status flips to 'paid', and next_date is advanced to 2026-12-02 - November skipped permanently, never projected into the register and never posted. This is the reviewer's failure mode, reproduced exactly, on a schedule shape the fix must not break. (A first attempt at this probe appeared not to advance next_date; that was my fixture's stale base_next_date, and correcting it produced the skip above.)

THE FIX, MEASURED END TO END through the real getHasTransactionsQuery, getStatus and advanceSchedulesService, same monthly schedule at next_date 2026-11-02, four scenarios, all passing: (A) transaction dated 2026-10-26, seven days early - the reporter's case - reports paid true; (B) transaction dated 2026-10-20, the reviewer's late-October case - reports paid FALSE and leaves next_date at 2026-11-02; (C) transaction dated exactly 2026-11-02 reports paid true; (D) transaction dated 2026-11-10, AFTER next_date, reports paid true AND advances next_date to 2026-12-02, preserving today's late-payment behaviour. Scenario B is the regression test the reviewer required and the one v3 fails; scenario D is why I rejected the reviewer's own option (a).

MEASURED PER-FREQUENCY window arithmetic, 7 of 7 scratch assertions passing: daily (interval length 1) grace 0, so occurrence 2024-03-10 -> 2024-03-10 and 2024-03-11 -> 2024-03-11, and a transaction dated 2024-03-10 satisfies ['2024-03-10'] and NOT ['2024-03-11']; weekly (interval length 7) grace 6, so start 2024-01-01 weekly at occurrence 2024-03-04 gives bound 2024-02-27, and a transaction dated 2024-03-04 satisfies exactly one of ['2024-02-26','2024-03-04','2024-03-11'], namely ['2024-03-04'], so adjacent weekly windows share no boundary; monthly and yearly grace 7; posts_transaction true -> exact occurrence date; one-time string date -> exact occurrence date; no date condition -> the existing 2-day lookback 2024-03-08.

WHY THE ONE-SIDED QUERY IS SAFE WITHOUT AN UPPER BOUND, stated as the mechanism rather than as a claim: the grace is min(7, interval - 1), so it is always strictly smaller than the recurrence interval. The lower bound for occurrence D is therefore never earlier than D - interval + 1, i.e. it can never reach the previous occurrence D - interval or earlier. A transaction late for the previous occurrence but dated within 7 days of D is indistinguishable from an early payment of D and is resolved in favour of D - which is the documented limitation in AC-3, not an unnoticed overlap. Meanwhile, because the query has no `$lte`, every date from the bound upward still matches, so a transaction dated after next_date is unaffected. The fix is a strict widening of an already-open-ended window by at most 7 days.

OBJECTION 2 RESOLVED BY CONSTRUCTION. Every case in tests[] now states its recurrence start, frequency, interval, patterns and endMode, and every expected bound is hand-derivable from `bound = D - min(7, intervalDays - 1)` with no recurrence evaluation at all: monthly start 2024-03-10 at occurrence 2024-03-10 -> grace 7 -> 2024-03-03 (MEASURED: this is exactly what the implemented helper returns); weekly start 2024-01-01 at occurrence 2024-03-04 -> grace 6 -> 2024-02-27; daily -> grace 0 -> the occurrence date itself. The reviewer's weekly example is corrected as they specified - start 2024-01-01, weekly, occurrence 2024-03-04, bound 2024-02-27 - replacing v3's impossible 2024-02-29. Because the bound is interval arithmetic rather than a reverse recurrence lookup, the skipWeekend and dual-rrule alignment questions v3 listed as untested unknowns cannot arise at all.

EXISTING-TEST IMPACT ESTABLISHED BY EXECUTION: running the fix against `yarn workspace @actual-app/core run vitest --run src/shared/schedules.test.ts src/server/schedules/app.test.ts src/server/forecast` gives 109 passed and exactly 2 failed, both in schedules.test.ts and both with their new values measured. (1) line 339 'uses exact date for recurring schedules with op is' - monthly { start: '2024-03-10', frequency: 'monthly', patterns: [] } at occurrence 2024-03-10 - expects 2024-03-10 today and returns 2024-03-03 with the fix. (2) The isScheduleOccurrencePosted table row 'early pay day before due for recurring date cond', transaction dated 2024-03-09 - expects false today and is inside the widened [2024-03-03, 2024-03-10] window, so it becomes true. The daily case at line 357, the one-time case and the auto-post case are unchanged. Every case in packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.test.ts passes with the fix, INCLUDING 'keeps a schedule posted today paid for the rest of the day' at line 989, which the reviewer flagged as needing an update if an upper bound were added - this plan adds none, so that test is untouched and is itself the guard against reintroducing one.

VALIDATION METHOD AND CLEANUP: temporary vitest files against the real exported Condition/RSchedule pipeline, the real getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate / getStatus / computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, and a real scratch database driving the real createSchedule and advanceSchedulesService, run with --disable-console-intercept because packages/loot-core/vitest.config.ts suppresses stdout console logs. All scratch test files were deleted and packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts was restored to its committed contents afterwards; `git status --short` shows only the untracked plan/ directory and `git diff --stat` is empty, so no application code was modified by this investigation.

REPRODUCTION MECHANICS worth recording for the implementer's QA: in the register the schedule row is NOT a table row. The schedule rows on the Schedules page are divs; the transaction rows in the register carry data-testid="row" with cells data-testid="date", data-testid="payee", data-testid="category", data-testid="debit". Clicking the date cell replaces it with a text input pre-filled with the current date, which you overwrite and confirm with Enter. Going to the register is done by clicking the account name in the sidebar. Waiting for the Vite dev server with `waitUntil: 'networkidle'` times out at 30s because the dev server never reaches network idle; use 'domcontentloaded' with explicit waits.

alternatives_considered.approach: The rejected v3 approach: derive the lower bound as previousOccurrence + 1 day by reverse-iterating the recurrence from a start shifted back one interval.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Measured to skip an unpaid bill. With a monthly schedule at next_date 2026-11-02 and a linked transaction dated 2026-10-20 (late payment of the October bill), the widened one-sided `$gte: 2026-10-03` reports the November occurrence paid and advanceSchedulesService advances next_date to 2026-12-02. The window is one full recurrence cycle wide, which is far wider than the 7 days needed to fix the reported bug, and it also carries a per-schedule recurrence lookup that v3 itself flagged as unmeasured at scale.

alternatives_considered.approach: The review's objection-1 option (a): keep v3's widened bound but give getHasTransactionsQuery an explicit upper bound, e.g. `$lte: schedule.next_date`.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer correctly notes it is not equivalent to today's behaviour, and the direction of the breakage is a regression, not a fix. Today a transaction dated AFTER next_date still matches, which is how a missed occurrence paid today reads as paid; MEASURED, scenario D (transaction dated 2026-11-10 for next_date 2026-11-02) reports paid and advances next_date to 2026-12-02. Adding `$lte` would make a bill paid a week late read as permanently unpaid - strictly worse than the bug being fixed, and it would break the existing 'keeps a schedule posted today paid for the rest of the day' case.

alternatives_considered.approach: The review's objection-1 option (b): keep exact-date matching for getHasTransactionsQuery and widen only the two-sided callers.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not satisfy AC-1 or AC-2. The Schedules page reaches 'paid' through useSchedules.ts:34, whose `liveQuery(getHasTransactionsQuery(schedules), ...)` feeds hasTrans directly into getStatus, so an unchanged getHasTransactionsQuery leaves the Schedules page reading 'Due' after the re-date - precisely the reproduced symptom. Only the forecast path would be fixed.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make the grace large enough to cover any plausible early payment, e.g. 14 days for monthly schedules.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It buys nothing for the reported bug (the reproduction is seven days) and starts to reach into the previous occurrence for weekly schedules, where the recurrence interval is only 7 days. The cap `interval - 1` is what guarantees disjointness across every frequency without having to reason case by case.

alternatives_considered.approach: Close the match window on BOTH ends, so a payment dated exactly on the previous occurrence's date counts toward the later occurrence too (v3's objection-2 option).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Measured by v3 to double-count: because posting creates the transaction dated exactly next_date, closing the left end too makes adjacent windows share a boundary date, so a transaction dated 2026-10-02 satisfies both ['2026-10-02','2026-11-02']. Same conclusion here, and the grace cap `interval - 1` makes the windows disjoint by arithmetic rather than by argument.

alternatives_considered.approach: Record which occurrence a transaction was posted from (a scheduleId + occurrence stamp on the transaction) and match on that instead of on dates.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Still the most semantically correct design - it makes every boundary debate moot, including the AC-3 limitation and the 7-day grace - but it requires a schema/migration change to the transactions table and touches every write path that can create or move a schedule-linked transaction. Far beyond a bug fix.

alternatives_considered.approach: Suppress the preview row purely because a linked transaction exists at any date, ignoring the date comparison entirely.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would let a transaction from six months ago mark today's occurrence paid, so a genuinely unpaid bill would never be projected or re-posted. That is the old-transaction guard the code comments explicitly warn about.

assumptions: monthUtils.currentDay() is driven by MockDate/setup in the loot-core vitest environment, so tests asserting behaviour around 'today' must set MockDate explicitly rather than rely on the system clock. In my end-to-end probes I set MockDate explicitly before calling createSchedule and advanceSchedulesService.
packages/loot-core/vitest.config.ts suppresses stdout console logs via onConsoleLog, so any test that needs to print diagnostics must run with --disable-console-intercept.

The date condition value on a recurring schedule carries `frequency` and an optional `interval`, as produced by recurConfigToRSchedule and by the demo fixture in packages/loot-core/src/mocks/budget.ts. The fix reads those two fields directly and does not need any other part of the value, so a value shape that omits them falls back to today's exact-date behaviour.

The nominal interval lengths used for the cap (daily 1, weekly 7, monthly 28, yearly 365) are deliberately the SHORTEST plausible spacing for each frequency rather than the average, so the cap errs toward a smaller grace: a monthly-on-the-31st schedule whose real gaps are 28 or 31 days still gets grace 7, and a leap or month-end irregularity can only make the real gap larger, never smaller, so `interval - 1` remains a safe upper bound on the window.

The $PREVIEW_URL app on this runner is the standard demo budget and the browser session is disposable; the reproduction created only schedule-posting state that the demo regenerates, so no cleanup of user records was needed.
unknowns: Whether 7 days is the right early-payment grace from a product standpoint. It covers the reproduced gap with room to spare and is asserted in tests, but the right value is a product judgement. The safety constraint is that it must stay below roughly half the shortest recurrence interval a schedule can have, which for a daily schedule means 0.

How the product should behave when a payment lands exactly on the previous occurrence's own date. A date-window fix cannot cover it without double-counting, and covering it needs a stamp recording which occurrence a transaction was posted from. Out of scope, stated inside AC-3.

Whether schedules whose date condition carries BOTH day-of-month and day-of-week patterns present any surprise, since recurConfigToRSchedule expands those into two rrules. This plan does not consult the recurrence, so the bound is unaffected either way, but I did not construct such a schedule to confirm the value shape exposes `frequency` as expected.

The per-schedule cost of the change is negligible - a table lookup and one date subtraction, replacing a constant - but I did not measure it against a budget with a large number of schedules, nor did I measure the app.test.ts scenarios against a large budget.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: The v3 plan was rejected on two grounds and I confirmed both by execution rather than arguing them away, then replaced the fix rather than restating it. Objection 1 - that getHasTransactionsQuery is ONE-SIDED so widening its lower bound admits a transaction belonging to the previous occurrence and can skip an unpaid bill - is CORRECT, and v3 does not answer it: v3 asserted disjointness, which is a property of the two-sided isScheduleOccurrencePosted and is meaningless for a `$gte`-only query. I proved the failure rather than restating it: I emulated v3's bound against the real Condition/RSchedule pipeline and the real advanceSchedulesService, and watched a monthly schedule at next_date 2026-11-02 with a late October payment dated 2026-10-20 flip to 'paid' and advance next_date to 2026-12-02, skipping November permanently, while today's code leaves it at 2026-11-02. I then rejected BOTH remedies the reviewer offered, for reasons I measured: option (a)'s `$lte: schedule.next_date` is a regression in the other direction, because today a transaction dated after next_date still matches and that is how a missed occurrence paid today reads as paid - I measured scenario D (transaction dated 2026-11-10) still reporting paid and still advancing, which an upper bound would have broken; and option (b) cannot satisfy AC-1/AC-2 at all, because the Schedules page gets 'paid' from the very query option (b) would leave alone, via useSchedules.ts:34. So the fix changed shape: instead of a window as wide as the recurrence cycle, the lower bound widens by a bounded grace of min(7 days, interval - 1). That cap is the whole answer to objection 1 - because grace is strictly smaller than the interval, the bound for occurrence D can never reach the previous occurrence, so the one-sided query is sound without an upper bound, and because the query has no upper bound every date from the bound upward still matches, so late payments keep working. I measured both halves of that claim end to end through the real service: the reporter's seven-days-early case reports paid, and the reviewer's late-October case reports NOT paid with next_date left at 2026-11-02 - the exact regression test the reviewer required, which v3 fails. Objection 2 - that v3's weekly worked example stated a bound its own rule cannot produce - is CORRECT: no weekly series has 2024-02-29 and 2024-03-04 as consecutive occurrences. But rather than restate the weekly case, I removed the class of error: because the bound is now pure interval arithmetic with no recurrence lookup, every expected value in tests[] is hand-derivable from `bound = D - min(7, intervalDays - 1)` with nothing to look up, and each case states its start, frequency, interval, patterns and endMode. The reviewer's corrected weekly example - start 2024-01-01, weekly, occurrence 2024-03-04, bound 2024-02-27 - is what tests[] now carries. Two of v3's open unknowns (skipWeekend alignment, dual-rrule expansion) disappear entirely, as does v3's day-loss trap with monthUtils.subMonths, because nothing in this design formats a month. I also established the existing-test impact by execution and named both changed cases with their measured new values (2024-03-03, and false -> true), and confirmed app.test.ts:989 still passes unmodified precisely because this plan adds no upper bound.
residual_risks: The 7-day grace is a product decision embedded in a single constant. It is asserted in tests so a change is deliberate, but a maintainer who widens it past roughly half a recurrence interval would reintroduce exactly the skip objection 1 identified, and the daily and weekly cases in schedules.test.ts plus the objection-1 case in app.test.ts are what would catch that.

The fix widens a window that getHasTransactionsQuery evaluates with no upper bound, and the two-sided isScheduleOccurrencePosted shares the same helper. Soundness now depends entirely on `grace <= interval - 1` holding for every frequency the interval table lists. Adding a frequency to the table without respecting that relationship would silently reintroduce the overlap; the table and the cap should be kept together, with a comment saying why.

I verified the four end-to-end scenarios and the per-frequency arithmetic in scratch files that have since been deleted, against a monthly schedule. Weekly, daily and yearly were verified at the window-arithmetic level but not through a full createSchedule/advanceSchedulesService round trip.

I could not verify the fixed behaviour in the browser, because the debugger role forbids editing application code. The qa_script browser steps are the implementer's to run and are the only remaining check on the end-to-end user-visible outcome.

The demo budget's 'Phone bills' recurrence starts at next_date, so the reproduction exercises a first occurrence. Schedules whose next_date has already advanced were verified only at the level of the reviewer-proposed November scenario, not in the browser.
